surroundingContext:
Gravity pulls objects toward Earth because Earth has mass and attracts nearby objects. When an object like an apple is unsupported, gravity causes it to accelerate downward. The apple does not move because it wants to go down; it moves because a force acts on it.

A spatial scene should make the invisible force visible. The apple, Earth, ground, and a force arrow are enough for the first version. Later, SPATAIL can add a path trail, a velocity arrow, and a comparison mode showing different planets.
learningGoal: Show why unsupported objects accelerate downward near Earth.
spatailPrompt:
Create an educational spatial explanation of "gravity pulls objects toward Earth". Learning goal: Show why unsupported objects accelerate downward near Earth. Prefer a cause effect visualization with labeled phases, progressive reveal, and interactive controls (step through, tap to highlight, isolate parts, reset). Use this surrounding context to identify the key stages: "Gravity pulls objects toward Earth because Earth has mass and attracts nearby objects. When an object like an apple is unsupported, gravity causes it to accelerate downward. The apple does not move because it wants to go down; it moves because a force acts on it.

A spatial scene should make the invisible force visible. The apple, Earth, ground, and a force arrow are enough for the first version. ".
